ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: At a bend on a highway, usually the road surface is higher on the outside and lower on the inside. As shown in the figure, on a certain section of road a car turns left, and the road surface on the driver's left side is somewhat lower than the road surface on the right side. The motion of the car can be regarded as circular motion with radius R. Let the height difference between the inner and outer road surfaces be h, the horizontal width of the roadbed be d, and the width of the road surface be L. The acceleration due to gravity is known to be g. To make the lateral friction force between the wheels and the road surface (that is, perpendicular to the direction of travel) equal to zero, the speed of the car when turning should be equal to (　　)

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: At a bend on a highway, usually the road surface is higher on the outside and lower on the inside. As shown in the figure, on a certain section of road a car turns left, and the road surface on the driver's left side is somewhat lower than the road surface on the right side. The motion of the car can be regarded as circular motion with radius R. Let the height difference between the inner and outer road surfaces be h, the horizontal width of the roadbed be d, and the width of the road surface be L. The acceleration due to gravity is known to be g. If the lateral friction force between the wheels and the road surface (that is, perpendicular to the direction of travel) is to be made equal to zero, what should the speed v of the car be when turning?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: on the left side of the figure is a photo of a car driving on a curved road surface; on the right side is a schematic diagram of the cross section of the road surface, drawn as an inclined plane that is lower on the left and higher on the right. In the schematic diagram, the angle between the inclined plane and the horizontal plane is labeled θ, the width of the inclined plane is labeled L, the horizontal projection width is labeled d, and the vertical height difference at the right end is labeled h, so the geometric relation in the figure is tanθ=h/d. Then reason: when the car turns left, the center of the circle is on the left side, and the problem states that the road surface on the driver's left side is lower and the right side is higher, so the supporting force of the road surface on the car is tilted left relative to the vertical direction, and its horizontal component can point toward the center of the circle. If the lateral friction force between the wheels and the road surface is zero, then the car is acted on only by gravity mg and the road surface supporting force N in the transverse circular motion. There is no acceleration in the vertical direction, so the vertical component of the supporting force balances gravity: Ncosθ=mg. The horizontal component pointing toward the center of the circle provides the centripetal force: Nsinθ=mv^2/R. Dividing the two equations gives tanθ=v^2/(gR). From the figure tanθ=h/d, substituting gives v^2=gR·h/d, therefore taking the positive car speed gives v=√(gRh/d). Final answer: v=√(gRh/d).
